author: Kate O'Connor
review_text:
We’ve tried this place three times and were disappointed every time. We’re honestly confused by the positive ratings.

The sushi misses the mark across the board. The spicy tuna seriously lacked flavor and was just tuna with a side of spicy mayo and oversized cucumber, and the rice was oddly sweet. Overall, it almost tasted like what you’d expect sushi to taste like if you tried to make it at home. The shrimp tempura had similar issues.

The house ramen also wasn’t good. The noodles were rubbery even after following the heating instructions, and the meat was strangely seasoned. Nothing tasted terrible, but everything tasted off.

Overall, this is a 1–2 out of 10 for sushi and ramen. If you seriously like sushi or ramen, this is not your spot. It’s unfortunate because it’s close by, but there are much better options elsewhere.

author: Jacqueline 5000
review_text: Visiting New Hamshire from Florida. Stopped for a quick back on my way to Boston airport. OMG. Delicious. You will not be disappointed. I had the Short Rib Ramen Bowl; the broth was so flavorful, and the short rib was so tender and juicy.

author: Megan Martin
review_text: The atmosphere is cozy and the people who work here were pretty nice. The food came out quickly. I really wanted to give this place a great review but I was disappointed by the food. The vegetarian ramen was super bland. Cold tofu on top and all the veggies were extremely plain and only boiled. No seasoning or sauce to give it flavor whatsoever. The mushrooms were super chewy and unappetizing along with the bamboo shoots. And I usually love eating both of those foods.  The only redeeming thing, food wise, was the matcha crepe cake which was okay and pre-made/refrigerated, but definitely not worth $8 a slice. The only thing I could think of while I was eating was the fact that I just wasted $30 on this meal.

author: Pearl Lee
review_text:
Koro leaves much to be desired, food and service wise. We eat a lot of ramen and were excited to see a Japanese spot open in Eastie; I signed up for the weekly specials newsletter as a reminder to go. Won’t hold to Tokyo standard, but will hold it to other ramen that we’ve had in Boston (e.g., Santouka (our go-to), Yume Wo Katare, and the place in Chinatown across from Asana Sushi that rebranded recently)

Service/Ordering :
• No wait to order and seat 4 around 7:30pm, though seating quickly ran out after. Would recommend for parties of 4 or less
• Several of us had questions on type of wavy/straight noodles used. Descriptions or photos would be helpful, because the wavy noodles turned out to be a non-conventional recipe.
• When I ordered miso ramen with wavy noodles, I was met with “oh I think they already come with wavy…nevermind it doesn’t say on the menu.” Staff should be more knowledgeable; I expect this from a student pop-up, less so from a restaurant that’s been open for more than a month. I’m just following the 1-2-3-4 ordering steps, it was choose your broth and then your noodles.
• I doubt many folks know what kukirage mushrooms are. Might be clearer to say “wood ear”, if you ever do a display revamp
• During ordering, it is unclear whether you still get a third free topping if you opt for a paid topping. Partner got the bok choy, mushrooms, and $1.50 egg, but should’ve been able to add a fourth.
• Kitchen was out of pork chashu two hours before closing, not a great look.
• Please offer your guests cups and/or a setup for free tap water
• Lights were lowered about 40% halfway into our meal even though it was ~8:15pm, far from 10pm closing time—mildly disruptive  to our table’s conversation but mostly just confusing for a second
• Most people’s attention is on the main menu when ordering and the weekly special flyer is easily missed. Just an observation.

Food:
• Chicken karaage was the highlight of the meal. Crispy batter without being too dry and good flavor on the chicken. The scallions don’t add anything when they’re underneath the chicken though, suggest leaving them out.
• Miso ramen: the shiitake mushrooms were cold and watery (they should be marinated), the noodles were oddly spongey (instead of chewy & bouncy), and the miso broth was a disappointment—sharp but also lacked flavor and umami, as if the broth was thrown together 30 min ago and wasn’t given time to meld. Curious what kind of miso was used. Portions of corn and mushrooms were generous but only two leaves of bok choy? Chashu pork belly was reasonable—could be more tender, but the flavor was there.
• Partner got the tonkatsu ramen. It was a thicker broth but still lacked flavor, as if flour was used to thicken it instead of aging pork bones properly. Was there any tare (seasoning sauce) added? He was similarly disappointed with the plain, cold mushrooms and $1.50 only netted half an egg.
• I acknowledge this is subjective but the ramen spoons are comically large. I initially thought they were spoon rests.
• I mean this in the nicest way possible, but perhaps consider lowering the frequency of your changing specials and focus on perfecting your mains.

tl;dr would come back for the chicken karaage, would not come back for the miso or tonkatsu ramen unless both noodles and broths are significantly improved. Recommend taking a couple pages from Santouka and reworking some of your recipes & processes if you want to build a following. I genuinely want the best for this shop; Eastie deserves to have good (East) Asian food!

author: Melissa Mahecha
review_text: We had a wonderful time at Koro Ramen & Sushi. It's exciting to have a Japanese food option in East Boston. The food was delicious, fresh, and very flavorful. We tried the veggie and shrimp sushi, and we will definitely be coming back!

author: Diandra Leigh Dente
review_text:
Koro is the new spot. From the moment you walk in, it's got that vibe – effortlessly chic, but still welcoming. You can tell there was thought and attention to detail about the whole experience.

The sushi is so fresh, it's insane. You can really taste the quality, and tell that everything's made with so much care.

Eastie has been needing a place like this, and Koro Ramen & Sushi is it. I'm so excited to have this restaurant in the neighborhood. It's not just a spot for food, it's a whole mood and so is Chef Harold.

author: Kevin Zhang
review_text:
As a sushi lover I was so excited to hear that this restaurant was opening in Eastie. Unfortunately, the food did not live up to the expectation.

The chicken karaage was good but the sushi was disappointing. I had the golden sunset and philly rolls. The fish did not taste very fresh, rice was not seasoned well, the mango was unripe, thin and leathery, and the roll quality was poor (see photos: not filled and pieces cut unevenly). Their specialty roll was so small, the same size as a basic maki despite being double in price. I do hope things improve so we can have some good Japanese food in East Boston.

author: Chenzhe Cao
review_text:
Koro Ramen and Sushi fills a much-needed gap in the Jeffries Point neighborhood, offering fresh sushi, hearty ramen, and flavorful poke bowls. I am so glad they opened since there hasn’t really been any good, healthy, and Asian spots. This restaurant focuses primarily on takeout, making it a convenient option for locals seeking good food without the fuss.

During my recent pickup order, I was impressed by both the value and quality. The poke bowl was generously portioned and well worth the price - clearly made with fresh ingredients that showcased the restaurant’s commitment to quality. The karaage chicken was a standout, featuring crispy, perfectly seasoned pieces paired with a creative chipotle mayo sauce that added a nice fusion twist to the traditional Japanese preparation.
While I didn’t have the chance to experience the dine-in atmosphere, the takeout process was smooth and efficient. The variety on the menu - spanning sushi, ramen, and poke options - gives Koro an edge in a neighborhood where fresh, well-prepared Asian cuisine has been hard to come by.

I hope to return soon and often!

author: Jeff Cannon
review_text:
We have eagerly awaited Koro’s opening! They’re a welcome addition to the neighborhood of East Boston. The restaurant is clean and bright, the tables are intimate, and the menu is easy to read on the wall. You order at the counter and grab a table. There are 5-6 tables and an outward-facing bar seating for 5 people. The single-use bathroom was clean and accessible. My wife and I had chicken karaage (app), a spicy tuna roll, and a crazy caterpillar roll. I felt it was good for the price! The app came out within 5 minutes; the rolls came out about 10 minutes later. They were busy and I still felt this was a reasonable time to wait for freshly made, counter-ordered food.

Give them a try!

Welcome, Koro!

author: Peter S
review_text: My first experience with restaurant ramen. Although it was good, I was a little disappointed in the noodles. I expected something much better than store-bought. These were better, but not a lot better. The veggies and protein were very good and just the right amount of spice. With the tip it was over $21 which seemed a little overpriced for earthy, working class, East Boston.

author: Josue Castillo
review_text: I’ve been waiting for koro to open definitely a great addition to east Boston! I had the koro roll, wings, B.L.T roll, miso ramen and the shrimp tempura, they were all delicious I highly recommend! Can’t wait to come back and try the rest of the menu

author: Brittany O
review_text:
This is a great new food option in Eastie. Very clean inside and we were able to get seats right away around 6pm on a Thursday.

I had the shrimp tempura roll and a build-your-own ramen. I thought the sushi was very good and a good size for the price.

I love the option to pick all your own ramen components. The tonkotsu broth was delicious and the pork belly was super tender.

I would highly recommend and I will definitely be back!

author: Stephanie D.
review_text: We tried Koro for the second time after trying them on opening week. The food was greatly improved this time- my partner really loved his ramen and I felt like mine was pretty decent. I love the atmosphere of the restaurant , it's so nice to have a place like this in Eastie. However, I found it really odd that they won't serve customers tap water to go along with their meal. For a sit down restaurant, I've never seen such a thing, and it left a weird impression, since the restaurant ambiance is so nice. At the least,  it seems like they would have a water dispenser. I will most likely come back, but likely because there isnt much competition for food like this right now in E Boston.

author: Ali Reneé
review_text:
I’ve been counting down the days until Koro opened & the ramen was even better than I expected! So many toppings to choose from and they FILLED the bowls 😋 - so worth it!!

The staff is also amazing and very friendly. When I walked in, I was handed a menu and got served very quickly - really great first impression before I even tasted the food!

I can’t wait to come back soon and try the sushi!

author: Eric Barron
review_text: I love some good Japanese food, especially sushi, so I was excited to try Koro as the only Japanese spot around me in East Boston.  I went my first time and ate in person and was underwhelmed by the maki rolls.  The rice was poorly seasoned and fish was okay.  I wanted to give it a second try a few weeks later and I got a few rolls for takeout and eating right away at the park nearby.  These were worse and the spicy tuna roll had an "off" taste that led me to not finishing it, and I don't like to leave food unfinished.  I did not get sick or feel ill, but I've been turned away from giving Koro a third try anytime soon.  I really hope they can turn things around because I would love to have a great Japanese spot in Eastie.  I'm rooting for you despite my experience.

author: Ana María García
review_text:
KORO is what we needed in the neighborhood, amazing ramen!! I loved the wings, soo crispy and tasty! I am a big fan of the edamame and the offer 3 different flavors which I loved!

Beautiful place and nice atmosphere!

Thank you!

author: Ethan Taylor
review_text:
Got sushi in May and all flavor was just hidden by above average-spicy mayo

Got Ramen in June and the chicken was as hard as a hockey puck

Got Ramen in August and the Pork was as hard as a hockey puck

Ramen broth is salty and I don’t want any spoonful of it

I like that someone monitors the reviews and hopefully adjusts. Best of luck

author: Christina Hathaway
review_text: I live in the neighborhood & have been so eager to try… well I tried it & it’s the best sushi I have ever had. I will be going back all the time!

author: Blake Aiton
review_text: Came from Maine for a conference and wanted some sushi. Googled near me and found this restaurant. Great little joint. Immediately greeted with a friendly hello, and service was great. Had  a dynamite roll, salmon and tuna nigiri and sushi. The place was clean and welcoming, and the sushi was awesome.

author: Juliet Clark
review_text:
I’ve given this place several chances, especially after winning a $100 gift card during their opening promotion. I really want to like it since it’s just around the corner, but I’ve left disappointed every time.

The tempura in the rolls is always cold, which makes me wonder if the shrimp and sweet potato are pre-fried and just sitting around before being added. The rolls themselves often fall apart, and the rice has that hard, slightly stale texture you’d expect from grocery store sushi, not what I’d hope for from a made-to-order restaurant.

I’ve only ever ordered takeout, so maybe the dine-in experience is better, but what I’ve had hasn’t left a good impression. I also tried the vegetarian ramen once, and it upset my stomach, and left me questioning if the broth was truly vegetarian.

Overall, despite its convenience and my initial excitement, this spot just isn’t for me.

author: Karen Liu
review_text:
I had a great dinner experience at this Legal Sea Food’s rooftop enclosed patio! It was hardly busy at all on a Monday night, so the place was quiet and very easy to talk. Our server was attentive and helpful.

We started with the fisherman’s platter, which consisted of a variety of fried seafood and veggies (onion, fries, coleslaw). The calamari was fishier than other ones I’ve had at restaurants, but everything else was tasty! We also ordered two soups: the clam chowder and the lobster bisque. The clam chowder was delicious, cheesy, and creamy. The lobster bisque, however, was weirdly caramel-y and off putting; we did not enjoy it.

Onto the mains, the prime rib cooked medium rare was delicious, and cooked just a bit more rare than expected but I actually prefer a rare/medium rare so it was great. The szechuan beans and mashed potatoes were also decent, they paired well with the steak. The other two mains (white fish and lobster tails) met our expectations as well, as they were tasty and well-portioned. The one main that we were let down by was the clam pasta (I forgot the specific name), but everyone thought it was overly sour, perhaps due to lemon?

Overall, we enjoyed a great meal at Legal Sea Foods; the atmosphere and service were both great and I would recommend this chain to anyone visiting Boston.

author: Tim Noonen
review_text:
We were in Boston for a couple of days and looking for seafood. We made reservations through open table and we were immediately seated near the back windows. The view of the harbor is amazing.
Our server was young and a little nervous, but super friendly and after a little conversation she relaxed and was really friendly and helpful.
We ordered the seafood tower for two and it was outstanding ... 4 oysters, 4 clams, 1/2 lobster, 4 shrimp, and tuna tartar. All were outstanding quality.
For the main course I selected the clams and my partner ordered the fettuccine with clams. My clams were good and cooked well, but i would probably order something else the next time. My partners dish was tasty, but a little heavy on the pancetta.
Overall, we had a great experience at Legal Seafood

author: Tiffany Nicole
review_text: This restaurant is a decent size with good service. I went for lunch around 2pm and it was slow we walked right in no reservation for a party of 7. Everything that was ordered was outstanding! Lobster mac and cheese appetizer down to the seafood platter, calamari, drinks were strong as well. The dessert cheesecake was also very delicious and authentic. You can tell everything here is super fresh it is a pricey restaurant but good and plenty of seating and a bar.

author: Avery Watson III
review_text:
Went Back For An Encore!
With all of the seafood choices in Boston, to opt for this restaurant twice in a 4-day vacation….says alot.  The seafood is obviously excellant.  But the ambiance is every bit as enjoyable.

We dined outside, among a cozy set of tables on the harbor.  It was a pleasant combination of relative seaside serinity and circus just inside.

I had and truly recommend the basic Fish and Chips.  Wifey selected the Crabcake& Shrimp, a signature dish for the restaurant.  Both were truly delicious.  We will definitely return!

author: Natalee Guerra
review_text:
Came in for lunch because we saw they had gluten-free fish and chips and were excited! We had an extremely uncomfortable experience here and will likely never return when visiting Boston. Overall, the food was ok for the price, but the service was not good at all.

We were sat instantly, however, it seemed to take about 10 minutes for us to even be acknowledged by our waitress. The restaurant was not very busy for a Sunday afternoon and they seemed to be perfectly staffed.

Initally, she just handed us waters with no introduction. She then came back around 10 minutes later and asked if we were ready to order to which we ordered the fish and chips. We then proceeded to be given gluten-free rolls which was awesome. The Guy who ran our food out, gave us more conversation than our waitress did the entire time.

I started to put my coat back on to show we were ready to leave. The waitress came over and asked if we wanted dessert, we declined and said we were ready for the check. To which she pulled out the machine for us to pay. We were planning on leaving a cash tip, however when my sister selected no tip the waitress immediately asked is there a reason why you selected no tip? It threw us off. I looked at her and said we were planning on leaving a cash tip to which her demeanor changed and her response was I take cash as well. I was extremely thrown off and just grabbed the loose dollars that I had in my purse which I gave to her. She counted in front of me and scoffed. She did not give us a receipt so I am unable to leave a name that explains how much service she even gave to us in the first place.

In my opinion, this is extremely inappropriate behavior from a waitress. We were hardly attended to in the first place yet to be asked this kind of question? I have never been asked why I wasn’t leaving a tip or watched while selecting the tip option. It was extremely uncomfortable. For the price of the food, the service should match and this restaurant did not meet those expectations.

author: Amy B
review_text: The yellowtail and the sole fish were wonderful. The oyster delicious- the freshness was just perfection. The clam chowder is not bad, but not the best there is. Definitely worth a visit for sure. Staff was helpful and gave good suggestions. Atmosphere was nice,  not so loud you can't hear the party you're with, but not super quiet. I love how is within walking distance to a variety of places.

author: Lisa Spenneberg
review_text: The atmosphere was like totally awesome! I did not get a picture of the oysters, we had four different types of oysters, yes it was the first time I've ever eaten an oyster and it was most awesome

author: Humberto Lameda
review_text:
I wasn’t sure about coming here at first since it’s a chain and I wanted an authentic Boston seafood experience — but I’m so glad I did. The clam chowder is fantastic and might just rival my long-time favorite She Crab chowder from Charleston. No wonder this soup is served at the Presidential Inaugural Luncheon every year!

I also had the swordfish — beautifully presented, satisfying, and full of flavor.
The service was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

Highly recommended!

author: Melanie Ponichtera
review_text:
We had the best experience at this Legal Seafood location than any other we’ve visited before! The entire wait staff was kind, accommodating and incredibly fast.
Our server was lovely and gave great recommendations. She was calm and patient with our questions and requests even though she had many tables and patrons.

The food was outstanding and the portions were fantastic. We started with the shrimp cocktail and it was so tasty for our first bite. Served with fresh lemon and a superb cocktail sauce, the colossal shrimp were cooked perfectly and were quite tender. Definitely a favorite for everyone! I didn’t get to take a photo, we got to them pretty fast!
Our kiddo had freshly sliced watermelon and a grilled cheeseburger and steak cut French fries. I had the Thai Peanut Salad with grilled chicken and it was such a delight. A generous portion, perfectly seasoned and grilled chicken and the flavor was everything I wanted it to be and more!
My husband had the baked stuffed lobster and it was better than he had hoped it would be. Plenty of food in the smaller portion which is about a 1.5 lb lobster, filled with bay scallops, shrimp crumbs and buttery goodness!!

We will absolutely be coming back the next time we are in Boston. Thank you to the staff of Legal Seafood for the lovely experience this afternoon.

author: Jenny P
review_text:
We visited this place because it was recommended by multiple people. We did not have to wait much to get a table and our server was the savior of the review ?and the bread).  He was amazing!!!!
We ordered fried calamari, it was good. We also had the clam chowder and it was very good too but I was honestly expecting something with more punch.
Reasons why the low rating:
- The sodas we ordered were flat
- Restrooms were not clean at all and very unorganized. There was no soap; all there was, was an empty liquid soap bottle with the top out. No drying towels.

author: Akin Ulusoy
review_text: This is hands down Boston’s best seafood spot. The lobster sandwich I had here? Best I’ve ever tasted! Loved it so much we came twice-if we’d stayed any longer, honestly, I’d have dragged you back every single day. Staff were proper friendly, kitchen smashed it, every dish was spot-on. Big thanks to the whole team-see you next time we’re in town!

author: Esther Mbiwan
review_text:
I love fish! I recently tried swordfish for the first time, and I have to say, I was not disappointed! It was tender, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. It's quickly become my new favorite. The food was amazing!
If you enjoy seafood, then Legal Sea Foods is the place to go!
I’ll definitely be back for more!!

The service was excellent as well.

author: Steven Briggs
review_text:
I loved the location and the service was great given how busy it was. They seem very responsive to food allergies which was helpful.
The food was good but what kept this from a 5 star experience was that the food was rather flavorless.  Even the salt/vinegar cod needed salt and has zero vinegar flavor.  It all looked great on the plate but I didn’t feel like I really got what I paid for. Maybe it was an off night but I felt at $200 (plus tip) for 4 people, that I overpaid a bit.
I hadn’t been to a legal sea food in maybe 12 years as my travel to the Boston area didn’t happen after moving to a different role at work.  I made a point of getting reservations months in advance and looked forward to the night.  It wasn’t like I remembered so perhaps that tarnishes the experience some.

author: T Y
review_text:
We recently dined as a family at Legal Seafood in Boston and were thoroughly satisfied with our experience. Seated on the terrace overlooking the harbor where the boats are moored, we appreciated the picturesque and pleasant setting. Despite the busy atmosphere and high occupancy, the ambiance remained friendly and warm, especially thanks to the proximity of the bar, the display of fresh fish, oysters, and lobsters.

The open kitchen demonstrated remarkable expertise and transparency regarding the quality of the products offered. This experience fully met our expectations for a seafood specialty restaurant. We highly recommend this establishment.

author: Anthony Lawson
review_text:
On my last evening in town for a work trip, our group of eight was looking for dinner in the Seaport area without a reservation, not an easy task. We decided to try Legal Sea Foods and lucked out when a no-show freed up a table for us right as we walked in.

The restaurant is large and was buzzing with activity. They also have a great patio that faces the harbor, perfect for an outdoor meal with a view. Since we had appetizers at a prior stop, we went straight to entrées.

Faced with a menu full of tempting seafood options, I asked our server for a recommendation of something local and fresh-caught. He suggested the North Atlantic haddock. I had never had haddock before, but I was impressed. It was perfectly cooked, meaty yet slightly flaky, with a clean flavor. It was served with rice pilaf, which was fine but forgettable, and steamed broccoli.

One of my co-workers ordered the lobster mac and cheese, and it was both impressive and indulgent. They use a full one-pound lobster, serving the mac and cheese inside the entire lobster shell with all of the meat mixed in. Highly recommended if you are not watching calories.

If you are in the Seaport area and need a solid seafood dinner without a reservation, Legal Sea Foods is worth keeping in mind, especially if you can snag one of those harbor-view patio tables.

author: Leonard Lim
review_text: Legal Sea Foods in Boston is a highly regarded restaurant chain known for its fresh, high-quality seafood and impressive wine selection. The Legal Harborside location stands out for its multi-level design, featuring a lively rooftop bar with scenic waterfront views. Signature dishes such as the New England Clam Chowder and Lobster Roll are must-tries. While it’s a renowned destination for seafood lovers, the diverse menu also caters to various tastes and budgets.

author: Jamme Ray II
review_text:
Went here with a group of 6 for lunch and we got seated almost immediately. Our server was super nice and our food times was very responsive. The seafood tasted really fresh and tasty. I got the Market Fish which was a Bass that day and the sides were the Szechuan Greenbeans and Bok Choy & Kimchi which were both good but the kimchi wasn't as flavorful as I was hoping. We also got Oysters on the shell that were really good  sharing! I had a Cucumber drink that was refreshing and I would definitely order again.

The place seemed fairly priced and the atmosphere was quite to where you could comfortably have a conversation at the table.

Would recommend to people to go for some good seafood.

author: Stan Kuleshov
review_text: Great spot with amazing seafood. The oysters were super fresh, the hazy beer was perfect, and the lobster roll really hit the spot. Service was awesome too — very attentive and detail-oriented without feeling over the top. Everything came out just right. Would definitely come back.

author: Shawn Shirley
review_text: Very good full service restaurant right on the harbor.  The food was delicious all around.  I tasted a lot from the party I was with and cant say I had anything I didnt like.  I personally ordered the lobster roll.  The roll was perfect with a healthy dose of lobster, yum!

author: Andrew Gummo
review_text: Legal Sea Foods in Boston was an excellent dining experience right on the water. The atmosphere was clean, relaxed, and well-managed, with efficient service from start to finish. We tried the lobster cone, buffalo shrimp cone, mussels in lemon garlic sauce, steak tips, and sole — everything was fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared. Prices were surprisingly reasonable for both the quality and the location. If you’re planning to dine in, definitely make a reservation — tables fill up fast. Highly recommend for seafood lovers visiting Boston!

author: David
review_text:
Visiting Boston for work, I knew I had to take advantage of being up north and finally try some truly fresh seafood—a big change from what I’m used to back home in Georgia. Luke’s Lobster ended up being everything I hoped for and more.

From the moment I walked in, the vibes pulled me in. The mix of easygoing music, a cozy atmosphere, and the kind young ladies working behind the counter made the space feel instantly welcoming. Even though the restaurant is small, it has a warm, home-like feeling—clean, quiet, and comfortable. If I lived in Boston, this would absolutely be one of my regular spots.

I ordered the seafood roll flight, which came with a drink and chips, and I couldn’t resist adding the lobster bisque. Everything was outstanding. The chilled seafood paired with the warm, buttery roll was a perfect balance—simple, fresh, and incredibly flavorful. Every bite felt like something I wanted to experience all over again. The bisque was rich, comforting, and full of that fresh lobster flavor you can’t fake.

Luke’s Lobster exceeded every expectation I had. For anyone visiting Boston—or lucky enough to live there—it’s a spot I’d highly recommend. Fresh, delicious, and full of great energy.

author: Greg Brown
review_text:
Hot Lobster Roll was perfect, friendly and just what you hoped for. Fresh bread, excellent soup as well.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Luke’s Lobster did not disappoint! The Hot Lobster Roll was absolutely perfect—packed with fresh, sweet lobster meat and served just the way you’d hope for. The roll itself was warm, buttery, and fresh, making each bite feel indulgent but balanced. The bread was outstanding, soft with just the right amount of crispness on the edges. Pairing it with their soup was the best choice—rich, flavorful, and exactly what you want on the side.

On top of the great food, the service was warm and friendly, adding to the whole experience. Everything felt fresh, thoughtful, and true to what you’d hope for in a classic lobster roll spot.

author: Peter Schimpl
review_text:
We dropped by Luke’s Lobster – Downtown Crossing and really enjoyed the experience. The place is quite small with limited seating, but that’s part of its charm — think “lobster shack in the city.”

The crab roll we ordered was vey good — fresh, tasty, and priced pretty reasonably for downtown Boston. The food came out fast (under 10 minutes), which was impressive considering how busy it gets. The service was friendly, fast, and professional, making the visit relaxed and pleasant.

Luke’s is located on Washington Street in the heart of downtown, so it’s perfect for grabbing a bite while you’re walking around the city or shopping. The interior is cozy and a bit tight, so many diners opt to take their orders and eat while walking or standing.

If you’re in downtown Boston and craving a solid seafood roll without the fuss, Luke’s is a solid pick.

author: Siaa B.
review_text:
This was my 1st time in Boston and according to several locals they highly suggested I try a lobster roll and this place is what they recommended.

I got the small portion since this was my 1st time trying it and honestly was glad I did but it wasn’t the most flavorful. The service however was lovely and the ladies at the front were so helpful. The location was tiny but was luckily able to grab a seat in a corner immediately after someone got up so I’d honestly prepared to grab your food and eat elsewhere .

author: Kris Promagan
review_text: Conveniently located near the Old South Meeting House, Luke's Lobster is a great place for a pit stop if you are walking the freedom trail. The lobster roll was amazing as was the clam chowder. The service was quick and friendly and they even bought my food to my table.

author: Quan Dao
review_text: Best place to get an affordable lobster roll in town! Great location + superb portion of lobster for the price. Go for the combo for the best deal ;) Highly recommend!

author: Hannah Williams
review_text: Stopped by Luke’s Lobster and it did not disappoint! Got the lobster flight which was buttery, simple, and delicious. You can really taste the quality. Perfect spot for a quick, satisfying seafood bite. Highly recommend grabbing the flight if you want to try a little bit of everything!

author: OH RR
review_text: These lobster rolls are better than any restaurant. Highly recommended. A must go if you're visiting downtown boston. They are understaffed so expect some waiting time.

author: Robin Metzger
review_text: Cheeky Lobster roll, very juicy, fresh, and buttery flavour. Got the smallest option for the lobster: 110 grams of lobster in roll with garlic butter, a pack or chips, and a drink all for $28. Think this is a great price to value if you want to try lobster roll as a snack during your walk through the freedom trail.

author: Sam C
review_text: Cute little pop in spot! We tried the lobster trio and the clam chowder. They were delicious and perfect bite size to share and try all the flavors. You get a good amount of lobster meat

author: Cory Edwards
review_text:
Luke’s continues to deliver on excellence. As someone gluten free I’m so appreciative of the options offered here. The GF roll is outstanding. I love to get the Trio sampler with mini individual Lobster, Crab, and Shrimp rolls. And they offer GF Lobster bisque! Hot! And delicious! Best lobster rolls I’ve found outside Maine.

——

Update August 2025: went to Luke’s again on another business trip. Man…just so so good. Had fantastic customer service too.

author: Mary Wiertelak
review_text: Literally such a yummy spot. Flight was so good I wasn’t able to get a picture before we finished one! Perfect snack to split with a friend. The guy who took our order was so nice and helpful too. Definitely worth the visit!

author: L
review_text:
$40 lobster flight comes with soda and chips

White truffle was good, but I realized that I like lobster very lightly seasoned, if at all. Lemon butter let the natural flavor of lobster shine the most. Spicy honey butter was okay

6oz meat is not a lot of food, it’s more of a tasting experience

Casual place for dine in, pay first at counter

author: Lauren Fasulo
review_text: Luke's was a great find, especially because they had gluten free rolls for myself! I got the 6oz Lobster roll on GF bread and I felt that they took extra care to prepare my roll for me. I also felt like it was a generous amount of lobster on my roll. The only thing I wish was that Lobster salad (mayo) was an option because I prefer that to the lobster with butter. Regardless, it was delicious and the staff was friendly! Definitely would go back.

author: Trina Shih
review_text: It’s just as delicious as the reviews say! The soda they offer is also very tasty and unique. There are three different sizes, each with a corresponding price. For a lobster roll, the price seems quite reasonable.

author: Shannon Travelingduo
review_text:
This place was very busy when I went. You get in line order and grab a seat. Wait for your order. I got the spicy lobster roll, came w chips and coleslaw. The coleslaw was subpar (my opinion). Also A soda. $52 The lobster roll
Was good (served in bread not a roll) , warm, spicy….. very good though not
The best I’ve had for the price point . I like James hook better- just my pers opinion.

author: Ronald Galati
review_text: First time in Boston and I had to get a Lobsta roll! Got a flight and the OG one so I could try them all. 1 was warm and all were delicious! Service was fast and friendly although cashier was a little too laid back. Food was like 4.5 stars, I bit a shell in the big OG 36$ roll which kinda sucked and it's a little pricy. Overall a great experience!

author: Ashley Harley
review_text: First time having lobster rolls. We did the flight to try several. Although we had nothing to compare them to, we thoroughly enjoyed the rolls, along with the glass bottled drinks and Cape Cod chips that were included. $40 for the flight of 3. Place is small but has indoor seating and right along The Freedom Trail. Kids had the hot dogs which were on the same bread as our lobster rolls and reasonably priced at $6 including drink and chips.

author: Luca
review_text: I’ve been to Luke’s Lobster places in Vegas and NYC but was eager to try it here in Boston closer to its origins in Maine. It didn’t disappoint. I had the combo rolls and clam chowder. The seafood was fresh and tasty and the clam chowder was great.

author: Bailey Mckenney
review_text: Quick service and more affordable option for a good lobster roll! I got the 4 oz, warm and I really liked the blueberry soda!

author: Abina Arthur
review_text:
Love Shake Shack and a special thanks to the people working there.

Toilets were dirty, they saw it and immediately cleaned it before we used them.

Service was quick, food hot and good as usual, what more do you want?

author: Pia Kehal
review_text: It's a surprisingly good burger for a fast food chain honestly! Patty was nice and crispy, bun was soft and warm and the salad was fresh and crisp. Lemonade was a good choice to wash it down with. Easy to order on the mobile screens and they call out your takeaway order or deliver it to your table number, plenty of seating available.

author: Christian Valera
review_text: I love this French Onion Burger is the best for me 😍🫶 The best burger, with the best quality bread, meat, and that special touch with the cheese and onions; it simply delivers an incomparable taste experience

author: Elyas Kopf
review_text: Typical burger classification, the burgers were mediocre in taste, nothing special. For a place in the city center, it's very clean, not many stupid people. Satisfactorily clean.The toilets are locked with a special code on your purchase receipt.

author: Tamas Bakos AC
review_text: It is among top 5 burgers I have ever had, with the single patty it is small though. Very delicious and juicy burger. The fries are better portion but the spice on it could have been more equally spread. Ordering at the kiosk is practical and they have table service. The recommended tip is set as default on 10%, that’s more than fair. Serving was fast and enough seating available even in rush hours.

author: Luke N
review_text: First of all, for a fast food restraunt, the burgers were so nice and the crinkle chips were salted nicely (not too much or too little). The burger was very meaty and had lots of fillings. The wait was very long, at around 30 minutes, which is very long for a fast food place. It was very loud and the service seemed rushed. It is conveniently located in the centre of Boston as well.

author: John Lambda
review_text: 4 1/2 stars. Good burger as always. Friendly staff. Not too crowded! Fill up before hitting the Freedom trail!

author: Melissa Abou Khalil
review_text: Went there for dinner with a friend. The service is great for how crowded the place was. Burgers are good but not that special. The fries are also good, not too oily.

author: Steve
review_text:
The burgers were really good.
It was difficult to find a seat, but we eventually did.
Service was quite slow.

author: Vicki L
review_text:
This shake shack does live up to its expectations except for one thing but they rectify it. The crinkle fries are extremely salty but they replace it and it’s hot crispy and tasty. The double burger ideas are real smashed burger. The burger is excellent, soft, hot, crunchy, tasty. It’s even better than the Guy Burgers (Guy Fieri).
This location on Washington Street is very convenient. It’s close to a lot of stores. The restaurant uses big and clean.
We will return.
5 stars.

author: Philomena Essex
review_text: It was our first time trying Shake Shack. We placed online order for pickup. Waiting time was long, place was busy, they seemed to be understaffed. Food was not bad, a bit above average, we liked loaded French fries the most. I would say it didn't meet our expectations or we were hoping to get more tasteful food. I would suggest to add extra staff for busy nights like that.

author: Nic c
review_text: Great location it's on the freedom trail just next to the tea party hall where plotting took place..I had the seasonal burger ordered at the self service kiosk. Lots of room. Consistent food quality.  Nice location to people watch taking the trail.

author: Shawn H
review_text: Regional management needs to come check this place out and assess customer service. Customers are forced to use the self-ordering stations. It was quite user-unfriendly and I couldn’t figure out why it was changing me an extra $9 for no reason. I asked a guy behind the counter and he told me I needed to figure it out. I then asked a girl who was on break; she is the reason I’m not giving this one star. The place was not very tidy. The burger was awesome, as I expected, but it took almost 30 minutes despite there only being a few people in the restaurant. The guys behind the counter were saying the F word very frequently and loudly horseplaying. A frat house environment. The shake came out after 10 minutes. It was okay. I won’t be back to this location.

author: Zack Eckley
review_text: If you're in Boston and craving a milkshake that's truly out of this world, you have to check out Shake Shack. While their burgers and fries are always a solid choice, the real star of the show for me is their milkshakes. I've had a lot of milkshakes in my day, but the one I had at Shake Shack was easily one of the best. It was incredibly thick, creamy, and packed with flavor. The balance of sweetness was perfect, not so sugary that it was overwhelming, but just enough to satisfy that sweet tooth. You can tell they use high-quality ingredients, and the dedication to crafting a great shake really shines through. If you're a milkshake lover, Shake Shack in Boston is a non-negotiable stop.

author: Holly Naimi
review_text: Im from iowa so we don't have these,  it's pretty good! Hot fresh and easy to get the order done and brought to us fairly quickly around dinner time on a Thursday evening.  Its expensive but its located downtown boston so to be expected.

author: Paul Vivas
review_text:
We ate in this Shake Shack this summer and were very happy with everything. This restaurant is one of our favorite whilst in the USA.
We always come back as we find the food to generally be good value for money versus other chains.
THis is particularly true in a very expensive city like Boston!

author: D L
review_text: I visited the Shake Shack in downtown Boston and I was seriously disturbed to see how our food was handled. A man with black gloves that he never changed put his hand in ALL of the food to be served to ALL the customers. Full hand with the dirty gloves on top of the XL fries and fingers inside the Burgers I guess to test the heat???? What are we DOGS????  WTH I quickly cancelled my food for my REFUND. They shortchanged me 5cents but I dont care. SEE YA I am DIGUSTED. I am sure a follow up generic comment will follow up with an email to contact your office. NO THANKS!!!!! People are getting sick in this country from nasty People. DO BETTER...

author: Adam Stippa
review_text: Ordered the Veggie Shack. Got a sad bun, lonely patty and some avocado trying its best. First try even came with… bacon. Plot twist I didn’t ask for. Not exactly plant-based dreams.

author: Lolo Disla
review_text: A very kind young man named Alex helped me and provided his service in the morning. He also gave me a great suggestion regarding the food. 5 stars for the food and for that excellent person.

author: Elyon Mark
review_text: Pretty clean and the service was good. The food is good. Well depends on what you get. I love the chicken burger. 🐔🍔

author: Christopher Vargas
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 4/5
“Golden Vibes at the Golden Cane”

The Raising Cane’s in downtown Boston—known as the Gold Cane—definitely lives up to its name. The gold theme makes the place stand out from the typical fast-food spots; it feels a little more special and modern, like a celebration of Cane’s itself. The decor is flashy but clean, and the bright gold accents give it a fun, upbeat atmosphere.

As for the food, it’s classic Cane’s—simple, crispy, and satisfying. The chicken fingers were fresh and hot, the Cane’s sauce hit just right, and the Texas toast was buttery perfection. The crinkle fries were solid, though they could’ve been a bit crispier. Service was friendly and quick even though the place was pretty packed.

The “gold” theme isn’t just for looks—it’s meant to mark this location as one of the flagship or showcase restaurants for Raising Cane’s, highlighting the brand’s best design and energy. It’s got that downtown buzz and a good mix of students, tourists, and locals grabbing quick bites.

Overall, the Gold Cane is worth checking out for the experience alone. Great for a quick meal, late-night stop, or just to see what a “gold standard” Cane’s feels like.

author: Anthony W
review_text:
Review of Raising Cane’s – 828th Location
Rating: 8.5/10

This location offered the most generous portion sizes I’ve ever received at any Raising Cane’s, making the price point feel especially reasonable for Boston. As someone who has visited over 25 Cane’s locations across the United States, I can confidently say this was the least clean among them. That said, the all-gold aesthetic and the unique sentimental value tied to it being the 828th restaurant add a distinct charm that sets it apart. Despite the cleanliness concerns, the visual experience and symbolic significance make this one of the most memorable Cane’s locations I’ve visited.

author: anant kumar
review_text: Straight to the top of my fast food rankings! The chicken was unbelievably tender, and those crinkle-cut fries might be the best I’ve ever had. Didn’t dig the sweet tea tho, should have gone for the lemonade

author: Y
review_text: Reasonable prices, no forced tipping, AND the waitress offered to throw out my trash?! In this economy, the fact that the food tasted good is the cherry on top. My only suggestion is to change your interior designer because it felt like I was dining at Trump Tower with all the gold...

author: bryan debarbieris
review_text: It's good overall. You know what you're getting when you come here and in my experience it's always been consistent. You can get varying sizes of chicken boxes with different numbers of strips. It's pretty much all they do. I get no slaw with extra toast. I got the caniac combo and it filled me up.

author: Treturus Savantur
review_text: Oh Canes… where do I began. I love Canes so much. The chicken is always crispy, the fries are well salted. The bread is warm and buttery. The sauce is immaculate. Wow! Don’t get me started on their SWEET Tea. Yum yummy yum

author: Adam Donaldson
review_text:
After hearing a lot of hype around this chain and especially people highly rating their "Cane Sauce" I was very excited to try it. But I left disappointed as it wasn't that great and I personally think Chick-Fil-A is a better fast good fried chicken chain.

Service was reasonable but the restaurant was generally loud and messy. We had a quick bite and got out.

Food wasn't great but also wasn't terrible.

author: andréa
review_text:
i live in europe and i heard a lot about how good raising cane’s was.. and they did not lie !! this is honestly the best fast food ever =D everything was good and i went there multiple times during my trip.
please open a raising cane’s in France !!!!

author: Dom
review_text: Cool golden interior. Food was pretty good. If there are any sweet tea enjoyers in Boston it is sold here.

author: Vicki L
review_text:
I have tried Cane’s at Las Vegas. The decorations are completely different from this Boston Cane’s. Both are about LOVE. The chicken tenders are for sure very tender and fresh. Their Cane’s sauce is the best. Check if they give it to you. It’s a must-have. The crinkle fries are average. The cole slaw is very smooth. The bread is very soft. Next time I’ll try their chicken sandwich.
Staff are efficient. It’s extremely crowded but you get your food very fast.
5 stars.

author: Anuj Bhatia
review_text: Good food and fast service,  middle of boston with gold theme amazing atmosphere

author: The Soto Standard
review_text:
I got the 3 tender combo with toast and fries, my wife got the same thing. We throughly enjoyed every bite and the ice in the drink is a nice touch. I also love the ketchup packets. The guy at the door welcomed us and even gave us a suggestion to use the self service to get our food faster (great host) anyways to be short.
Great Food, Excellent Customer Service , Very Clean and Spacious Environment. Got my food in 5 mins regardless of the huge line out of the door. I entered and the guy welcomed me immediately. For a fast food spot this specific Raising Canes Is And Should be the Standard for Fast Food Done Right!!!

author: Eric Perez
review_text: This was my first time trying Raising Cane's and I really enjoyed it. I got a combo box with 4 tenders, fries and sauce, usually comes with coleslaw as well, but I'm not a big fan of 'slaw', so I got extra fries. The chicken was really delicate and flaky, almost like it was fresh. The fries were, just fries and the toast, didn't even pay attention to it, but it was fresh and crispy on one side, but not the other. The sauce was really good, I even dipped my fries in it and made them a little better. The place is all gold as well because it opened on the 28th of August, so Golden Birthday. Overall, the place was clean, it was busy, but I only waited about 5 minutes for my food and it was good. Overall 7/10, got Eric stamp of approval!

author: Timothy Grace
review_text: It's pretty good food, and priced VERY well. It can be a bit messy to eat, but such is the nature of these things. The music was very loud, as was the restaurant as a whole, which detracted from the experience in my opinion. The price my lure me back here, and the food is good enough to make it worth it.

author: Shelby Vandewalle
review_text: Love the everything gold aesthetic. The staff is really friendly and helpful. My order came out fast. Although I did come here on a weekday. Ordered a three finger combo. Came out just as I wanted. Worth checking out.

author: Kay Foulkes
review_text:
The only downside was the bathrooms which only had hand sanitizer.

Lived the gold theme of the restaurant and the food was some of the best fast food we had visiting the states.

author: Nat E
review_text: Such a cool concept! Everything is gold! Just wish they had some gear to buy in store to take as a souvenir for us visitors. The service was not as great as what I am used to in Texas, where I live but it was ok. Food was also not as fresh but I came in at 10pm (they close at midnight) so maybe that’s why? Overall I would recommend to visit just to check it out if you happen to be in the area.

author: beni
review_text: I recently visited the Raising Cane's in Downtown Crossing, Boston, and overall, the experience was great! The chicken fingers were perfectly crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor—exactly what you'd expect from Cane's. The signature sauce paired with the Texas toast and crinkle-cut fries made for a very satisfying meal. What really stood out was the decor. The restaurant was decked out in gold accents, which gave it a fun, upscale vibe—definitely not what I expected from a fast-food spot. However, the one downside was that I had a hard time finding seating. The place was packed, and the seating area seemed pretty limited for the size of the crowd. It would have been nice to enjoy the meal in a bit more comfort. Overall, still a great spot for some delicious chicken, just be prepared for a possible wait if you want to sit and eat inside!

author: Jessica Schneider
review_text: Raisin cane chicken fingers are so juicy and delicious. They melt off bone good. The service wasnt clear what i ordered. While waiting, it was a bit hectic. I was disappointed that $9 didnt get meal. It was only the chicken. It goes in the splurge fast food section.  It's def worth it.

author: Ashley Chance
review_text: My picky daughter even loved it. Fast, friendly, and absolutely delicious.

author: Meka Simms
review_text: I don’t know how this place has 4.8 stars Tacos were horrible. The lettuce were wilted and soggy. They got my order wrong. I order the super taco and got regular tacos. I gave one star only because the potatoes were good.

author: Nau Como
review_text: It was my first time eating at Taco John’s and it didn’t disappoint! The place was super clean and had a cool vibe! The chicken was fresh, flavorful, not greasy, and packed with just the right amount of seasoning. The Potato Olés were so good—crispy, perfectly seasoned, and addictive. The service was quick and friendly, making the whole experience even better. Whether you're craving a classic taco or a hearty burrito, this place hits the spot!

author: Hussaim
review_text:
I just had the best experience at Taco John’s in Boston! From the second I walked in, the vibe was super chill and welcoming. The staff were friendly, which always makes a big difference, and the place itself was clean and comfy.

Let’s talk about the food—honestly, it was amazing. I got the tacos, and they were so good! The seasoned beef was perfect, and the crunchy shell with all the fresh toppings made every bite satisfying. I also tried the Potato Olés (because why not?), and I have to say, they’re a game changer—crispy, loaded with flavor, and just the right amount of seasoning.

The menu has a great variety, so you’ll definitely find something that hits the spot no matter what you’re craving. And their salsa bar? Big fan. It’s perfect for adding that extra flavor kick.

Plus, the service was fast and friendly—always a plus when you’re hungry. I’ll definitely be back next time I’m in the area! Highly recommend this spot if you’re looking for a quick, tasty meal.

author: Susie Li
review_text: I ordered catering from Taco John's in Boston for a big meeting at work, and I couldn't be happier! We needed 100 burritos with some specific survival food restrictions, and they went above and beyond to accommodate all our requests. The food was absolutely amazing—fresh, flavorful, and satisfying. Everyone loved it! The staff was super friendly and professional throughout the process. I'll definitely be ordering from Taco John's again for future events. Highly recommend!

author: The Soto Standard
review_text:
Great Customer Service.
Solid food but I could feel how cold some of the ingredients were before I ate it.
I also had trouble with ordering on the tablet because there was so many customization items that I accidentally added an extra side of sauce.
Other than that, my experience was great.
Best Comparison : If Burger King and Taco Bell had a child !

author: Brad Loncar
review_text:
The service was super friendly, fast, and helpful.
Really appreciate that. The tacos are very thin and look (at least mine) nothing like the photo. The potato olés have a good flavor.

author: gochase85
review_text: Grand opening of Taco John’s in Downtown Crossing.  So much better food than the Door Bell further down the street. Friendly staff, great food and great location.  Can’t wait to try the Fish Tacos next time!!! 👍👍

author: Susie Li
review_text:
I just found the best tacos in Boston at Taco John’s! They use fresh, high-quality ingredients — you can actually taste the difference in their sauces and meats. My favorites are the Boss Bowl with steak, cheesy quesadillas, and the spicy jalapeño burrito — perfect for heat lovers! Don’t miss the churros — only $3.49 and 6 inches long! Plus, they have amazing deals, especially on Taco Tuesday — tacos under $2!

If you want Mexican-inspired fast food made with care, come to Taco John’s. Trust me, I’m now a total taco fan!

author: Joy James
review_text:
Taco John’s just opened this past Thursday in Downtown Crossing, and I’m really impressed. Opening a taco spot right across from Taco Bell is a bold move, but they absolutely deliver.

The food is incredibly fresh, hot, and full of flavor. Everything I tried was delicious, and it came out really quickly. The staff was kind and helpful, and the bathrooms were very clean — always a good sign.

I’ll definitely be back. It’s a great new addition to the area, and totally worth checking out.

author: R C
review_text:
★★★★★

Taco John’s absolutely blows Taco Bell out of the water! This place is a fantastic addition to downtown Boston—finally, a fast-food taco spot that delivers on quality and flavor. The service is top-notch, with friendly and efficient staff who make sure your order is perfect every time. The food is fresh, fast, and absolutely delicious. The tacos are loaded with flavor, the Potato Olés are addictive, and everything tastes like it’s made with care. If you’re looking for a quick, satisfying meal that doesn’t sacrifice quality, Taco John’s is the place to go. Highly recommend!

author: Mohammed Elkholy
review_text: Prices are insanely good. A full meal for just $5! Totally recommended.

author: Chef Champ
review_text: Cool spot with affordable prices. They have daily specials and taco Tuesday prices. The only issue which may not be a big one is the taco meat has no flavor. You definitely need to use the sauce packets for an extra boost. But the potato oli's are 🔥🔥🔥

author: Jose Lopez
review_text: Delicious Mexican food and very affordable for the amount of food per dish definitely will fill you up. 10/10 Would recommend to others in the future.

author: Dwayne Sturdivant
review_text: And ask for extra everything I paid for  it and it looks like this I want my order re made or my money money back this this nasty

author: Sarah Jane
review_text:
After leaving the midwest, this was the chain I missed most, the absolute joy I have that this food is close by again.
The location is great if you use South Station, the employees were all incredibly nice, the place was clean and bright.
The food? Just as good as I remembered, everything was made in incredible time, it was hot and wonderful. They even had some gluten free options for my sister!
This was the PERFECT place to catch up with old friends and reminisce. I will absolutely be back!

author: Ashby H
review_text: Very friendly staff. The atmosphere in general was pretty overstimulating, and the food had little to no flavor, other than grease and salt. I felt sick after eating one taco

author: Anthony C
review_text: First welcome to downtown Boston, growing up in the Midwest allows me to become familiar with Taco Johns and im so glad to see you all finally open up!  The prices that im used too are alittle lower but this is Boston so the price of everything I ordered was fair.  Service was excellent thanks for being so welcoming!  I will be coming back again !

author: Shelly Ja
review_text: My first time trying Taco Johns. I had a great experience here. Clean place first of all, kind and attentive employees. Ease of ordering, order came out quickly and I was on my way. The taco salad is actually pretty good! Soft chicken taco was yummy with good flavor, love the diced chicken pieces inside.

author: Edward Park
review_text: Food not bad, I just put Taco John's behind Del Taco, Taco time and, the Bell. Restaurant interior is very nice, enjoyable to spend time there.

author: A V
review_text: My husband and I were shopping downtown for our vacation and walked by this place, so we decided to stop in and check it out. We were greeted by one of the gentlemen at the door, ordered our food, and waited less than five minutes for it to be ready. Everyone was friendly. We dined in, and the food was fresh and delicious. We had a boss bowl along with chicken tacos and potatoes oles with nacho cheese sauce, all of which were very delicious. 10/10. One of our chicken tacos tasted like fish, so my husband asked if it was chicken or fish, and they confirmed it was chicken but also gave us a new taco at no charge. The food was very delicious, and we will be stopping by again. Congratulations on your new journey. 🎉

author: Fang Phattha
review_text: A nice bakery shop near South Station. They have free wifi and a lot of seatings. It's very nice sitting by the window looking at people walking by. This somehow took me back to London so it's very nostalgic. Breakfast was good, although I think it's a bit bland. The restaurant looks new and clean but restroom was noticeably quite dirty when I went, unfortunately.

author: Christian Gladwell
review_text: Tatte Bakery & Café on Summer St is an amazing spot for breakfast or a mid-day pick-me-up. The pastries are always fresh, the coffee is rich and smooth, and the atmosphere feels warm and welcoming. The staff is friendly and efficient, even during the busy hours. A perfect place to relax, work, or catch up with friends.

author: Jim Murphy
review_text:
Solid place to eat today after the No Kings Rally at Boston Common on an amazing Fall Saturday in Boston!

Walking back to South Station, Tatte was a perfect place to stop to rehydrate and have some food before a train ride home.  The cold water station was greatly appreciated; no coffee on this visit, but i look forward to it next time!

We each ordered a sandwich and can of tonic, with a dessert to split.  The water station was also greatly appreciated.  Then we went on our way home on the south shore.

author: Pinar DİKENSAK
review_text:
Tatte feels like one of Boston’s signature cafés — cozy, vibrant, and full of character. The scrambled eggs and fresh mozzarella sandwich were fresh and tasty, and the bread was excellent. It’s also a family-friendly place, which we really appreciated.

On the downside, it gets very crowded and noisy during peak hours, and the service can feel a bit rushed. Prices are also on the higher side.

Still, it’s a must-try spot if you want to experience a true Boston café atmosphere

author: Aleksandra Krzywoń
review_text: Probably the best spot for breakfast in Boston! The place is spacious, bright, and really pleasant to sit in. And the breakfasts? Absolutely delicious! I especially recommend the shakshuka – it’s a definite must-have here. We also tried other dishes from the menu, like the salmon and chicken bowls, as well as the salmon, avocado, and scrambled egg sandwich – everything was really tasty. But the shakshuka is what truly stood out and will stay with me for a long time. If you’re looking for a great place to enjoy breakfast – alone or with friends – this is it!

author: William Lau
review_text:
Great place to hang out. Pastries look good. We only had drinks, no food unfortunately.

Americano was a bit on the sour side but not bad.

Ginger Date Oat Milk Latte tastes good but is probably without coffee as it was so white colored and no coffee taste.

No parking I can see and it's the urban center.

I would visit again as it is so close to South Station.

author: SGT
review_text: The good: I want to move to Boston just so I can come here regularly. I ordered the blueberry beet ricotta salad. The dukkaah was to die for delicious! This salad was by far the most scrumptious dish I’ve eaten this week. It’s a good thing a small roll (perfect size) was included because I would have ended up licking the plate instead of sopping the plate. I would have enjoyed more beets though. Now that unpleasant side: seating. The place was packed! A great sign of its deliciousness, but I was concerned I wouldn’t get to sit and savor my salad. All in all i give this 10 stars and would give anything to eat here again. Don’t judge the salad by my photo. It has already been half devoured by my sister who barely saved me a bite. 😆

author: Foodstaham
review_text:
Great hang out spot that opens early with food, sweets and coffee ☕.

Even though it's a very busy Cafe, servers are friendly, you don't have to wait long for your order, and everyone seems to be having a good time.

Bakery items are given to you right away at the cashier.
If you're sitting for food or coffee, they'll give you a number to take to your seat.
They'll come find you when it's ready.

Bar style seating is available at the windows, which is perfect for people watching.

Outdoor seating is available, just watch out for pigeons.

Ratings:

Flat white 7/10
It has an equal balance of milk and coffee flavor so you can still taste the coffee. The coffee itself taste like a light roast with some nutty notes. The texture is smooth and velvety.

Passionfruit Krembo 6/10
It looks amazing, but it only tastes ok because the passionfruit is hidden. Instead of passionfruit flavor you get a lot of plain sugar flavor. The cookie on the bottom doesn't help it's a sweet sugar cookie. The outer yellow layer is like a candy coating, the white cream inside of that is just like whipped cream. Hiding under those layers is where you will finally find the passionfruit- a yellow/orange jelly with all of the flavor that you wanted.

Pistachio croissant 6/10
The outside isn't as flaky and soft like a really good fresh croissant but the pistachio flavor inside is decent.

author: Amy T
review_text: So happy to stumble upon this place, the name drew me in, the bright airy space with the welcoming staff made me want to stay. Excellence at every level and some of the most delicious and visually pleasing homemade baked goods around. Total nachat-fest for me. Happy to give them my shekels! Next time I’m going to try the food. Hazak u Baruj! Love at first bite 😉

author: Sofia Fesenko
review_text: The shakshuka was big and delicious, and the sandwiches were just as impressive—fresh and full of flavor. The coffee was good, though not particularly standout. Overall, a great spot for a tasty and satisfying meal.

author: elizabeth s
review_text: Got a brownie $4.50 and a flatbread for $6.50. Both tasted excellent, would definitely go again. The atmosphere was great too, lots of space to sit, work, hang out. They put a lot of effort into the branding and it looks great.

author: Emma C
review_text: Looks pretty nice inside, love the decor. The food is definitely overpriced I got the passion fruit cream thing which wasn't that great and was very hard to get it off the plate to eat. Bathrooms were pretty clean and there was a lot of people, pretty popular place.

author: sesha sai srivatsav
review_text: Tattes menu is excellent and taste is great! Highly recommend. Wish the items were warm. I get it they’ll wait for order to be ready to be served. But overall good!

author: Miriam Alvizures
review_text: Yum! 😋 delicious!! The food was warm and inviting. The drinks were refreshing and filled our hearts with joy. The seating area was very tranquil. Great for people watching. Love.

author: Aryella Almeida
review_text: Lovely place! Great tea, great latte. Pistachio croissant was amazing. Savory was good but ask them to warm up. 😉

author: Jordan Anderson
review_text: I’ve tried many coffee shops in Boston but always find myself returning to Tatte, particularly when I’m looking for more than coffee. The drinks are excellent. But the food sets it apart from pastries to hot breakfast items. All in a clean, modern farmhouse setting.

author: traveler
review_text: I ordered a black sesame latte, Jerusalem bagel, and a tiramisu. Never had a Jerusalem bagel so I was very curious, and it was good! Has a very cozy yet lively vibes. Love all the interior designs. Would have to come back to try more things! Service wasn’t too bad.

author: Madeline Cook
review_text:
A lot of their food is pretty good—it’s not amazing, and it’s on the pricier side for what it is, but it’s pretty good.

However, the service, in particular at this location, is absolutely terrible. I can’t believe how rude and unhelpful they are!

I stopped by for lunch today and ended up leaving without order anything because the person at the counter was so difficult I couldn’t even place an order with her. I asked for a simple substitution (halloumi instead of chicken) and she literally rolled her eyes at me!

author: Caitlin M
review_text: This bakery is lovely !! Super friendly staff and delicious food! Super delicious and tasty will definitely be back!

author: Rachel Reyes
review_text: The coffee here is really good! I love that the breakfast options feel a little bit on the healthier side! I definitely wish it was a little bit more organized, and helpful by the staff but overall I didn’t enjoy coming here and it’s definitely a staple in Boston! 🫶🏼

author: Fang Phattha
review_text: A lovely food court near South Station. They have a lot of seatings. Most people here seem to be office workers looking for lunch. The vibe is quite nice and not rushing. I had a DIY bowl from a healthy place with a long line that I can't remember the name. It's very fresh and very delicious. Ingredients are already seasoned and go well together. I'd give it 5 stars if there are more variety of food to choose here.

author: Jane Sh
review_text: Excellent and very stylish and beautiful place, looks like a food court with a large number of different restaurants, from sushi to halal cafes, there is also Mexican and Indian cuisine and many others, there is a bar where you can drink beer and eat fresh oysters, in general a complete variety. The sushi was great, we also ordered shawarma with halal chicken, we also really liked it. I recommend this great place

author: J. Yeh
review_text:
This is a wonderful hidden area for a lot of great food choices. Great area for lunch.

My brother got oysters from a raw bar, and I got a fried chicken sandwich and sweet potato fries from Hailey Jane's. There are many other foods like, pizza, sushi, Mediterranean, Indian, drink bar, etc.

The area is spacious with many seating tables, and has a very nice atmosphere with natural lighting.

It's also very close to the red line South Station T station.

author: rossana urugutia
review_text: We enjoy this food halls when we want a bit of different food, a change for our tastebuds. More of a mature food halls than others in the area. Always stop by when we are in Boston

author: Michael Allen
review_text:
High Street Place is a fantastic food hall with a wide variety of options all in one spot. The atmosphere is modern and lively, making it a great place to grab lunch, dinner, or even just a drink. There’s something for everyone, whether you’re in the mood for casual bites, creative cocktails, or more elevated dishes. The layout makes it easy to explore different vendors, and the quality across the board is consistently strong.

It’s also a convenient location right downtown, perfect if you’re visiting nearby attractions or just want a fun, social spot to eat. A great mix of local flavor and variety under one roof.

author: Gabbie Kim
review_text: I enjoyed eating at this food court. There were so many options to choose from—pizza, burgers, sandwiches, Mexican, Indian, Japanese, Mediterranean, and even a café, just to name a few. The food was decent and reasonably priced. We went during lunchtime, so it was quite crowded and hard to find seats. I would visit again.

author: Simon McAuliffe
review_text: Great vendors. The cocktail bar (Daisies and Daiquirs) is amazing. You can lots of different types of food, so it is great for meeting up with people who have a variety of tastes.

author: Shali S
review_text: Second time I’ve been here. Love it. So many options are available for food. All the restaurants are worth trying. Already planning on returning soon.

author: Tomas Piaggio
review_text: Awesome place in Boston, with great food options, nice beer and cocktails, plenty of space to go with a big group. The music is not loud so you can chat without any problems. Will definitely come back!

author: Chimere oronzi
review_text: The food hall has a variety of foods to offer. It's cute and surprisingly very clean. We went to Mike and Patty's because we saw they had vegan options. My husband got the vegan Burrito, and I ordered the vegan classic. Firstly, the girl working gave me a regular egg and cheese, so I took it back to explain that I requested to make it vegan. I didn't like her response and tone when I tried to have my order corrected. Telling me that I didn't order a vegan sandwich. When I sure wouldn't have ordered a regular one because I don't eat regular eggs. That is why I rated the service with 3 stars. The rating does not apply to the entire food hall and other vendors. Just my encounter with the employee from Mike and Patty's.

author: A R
review_text: High Street Place is a fancy food court in the financial district / seaport area of Boston. We stopped by here for some after dinner coffee and dessert. This food court is very nice and highly recommended if you live in or are staying in the area!

author: Alexander Ly
review_text:
Several food options. We are at Mike and Patty's where I ordered the MBB burrito. It's made fresh, though tastes like it looks. Tortilla, avocado, and eggs.

My wife and son ordered the Crack sandwich 🥪. Good and cheesy, but must eat while hot; otherwise, the cheese cools down.

author: Laurence Jackson
review_text: Such a fun spot for an evening! We did trivia on a Tuesday, but check out live music, sports or family programs!  Melbourne laneways maybe inspire this  use of commercial space.

author: Ciara T
review_text: We had to go to the Japanese Consulate and were so happy to find this food hall right next door. The food was really good and it seemed very clean and new. There weren’t a lot of people in the middle of the day. I’d love to try all the restaurants.

author: Jimmy B
review_text:
Not a bad place to eat, drink and have fun, although not as much of a selection as Time Out Market. This place offers a more sophisticated approach to mall dining .

Pizza, pasta, bar food, Mexican, ice cream, alcoholic drinks and even a champagne vending machine.... What more could one ask for??

PRO TIP: grab the chicken nuggs from HALEY JANES (be careful of the spice kick 🔥) and combo it up with the Mac n cheese from PENNYPACKERS
Then, Grab a cocktail from the professionals at DACQUIRIS & DAISIES
After ice cream time!
And you've got yourself a nice date.

Tenderoni slice was not bad but very small for the price tag of 8$ (tasty slice tho)

author: Sarah
review_text: Really awesome selection of food. Lots to chose from which makes it fun. The downside is that it can get very busy and feels like a small space.

author: Alain Lafume
review_text:
I went to high street place to have a few drinks and the varieties were plentyful enough. I had two kinds of beers. One blueberry 🫐 and another some kind of creamer one.

I had a good time with my friend. Would go again. Though I might try some other kinds of drinks.

author: TANIA RODRIGUEZ
review_text: The food hall atmosphere and the food options are super good! If you are a group, everyone can order exactly what they want! Experience worldwide food in just one place! Sushi, Pasta, Sandwiches, Tacos, Hamburger, Hand made Juices, Salads, Pizza, MOET champagne, Coffee, Cocktails… Saturday afternoon DJ is fantastic for enjoying a beer! I love this place for the options and vibe!😉

author: Irvving Kairos
review_text: The rain helped us stumble upon this place. Before walking in, we did not hear about it nor saw any type of advertisement in Boston. But it was a pleasant surprise tucked in the middle of buildings. Offering a variety in different shops, food and drinks, this food hall did delivered. The lounge area was buzzing but sadly the food halls seemed ghostly. Don't know if the set up is to blame for, but it provided a nice space for a bite, some drinks and a chill place to hang out with friends and family.

author: Esmeralda Isufi
review_text: I had a great experience at Noble Castella! Their katsu sando is absolutely delicious! And the desserts are heaven 🤤

author: Jasmine Caez
review_text:
We dined here on Christmas evening and had an exceptional experience. Despite how busy the restaurant was, our server remained attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming throughout the night. He would pop in on us constantly to see if we needed anything!

The food was outstanding from start to finish. The warm bread served at the beginning was so good we had to stop ourselves from eating too much before the meal. We ordered the Surf & Turf for 2 with mac and cheese for our side, and everything was prepared perfectly. The steak was cooked just right, the lobster tail was tender and flavorful, and the mac and cheese was rich and well-seasoned.

We ended the evening with the coconut cream cake, which was unique and absolutely delicious. Unlike anything we’ve had elsewhere.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience, and we would happily return. Thank you for making our Christmas dinner memorable.

author: Alexis Sabbaghian
review_text: Smith & Wollensky Boston never disappoints. We shared the porterhouse steak — perfectly cooked and full of flavor — along with creamed spinach, fried onions, and mac and cheese that were all spot on. Finished with a rich, crackly crème brûlée that tied everything together. The food, service, and classic atmosphere make it one of those places we just keep coming back to.

author: Gabbie Kim
review_text: It was okay overall. I’ve had better steak, but it definitely wasn’t the worst. The seasoning seemed uneven, so the first half of the steak tasted pretty bland. The place was packed on a Wednesday night, and while our server was clearly busy, they only checked in at the very end, and our water sat empty most of the time.

author: Steven Chen
review_text:
I’ve always enjoyed dining at Smith & Wollensky and most parts of my recent visit were great the service, the atmosphere, and the rest of the dishes were all solid.

However, I was really disappointed with the Wagyu Ribeye. For a steak that costs $150, the experience fell far below expectations. I waited almost an hour for it, and the first one that came out was extremely salty. After sending it back, the replacement steak arrived noticeably undercooked. I had ordered medium, but as you can see, the doneness was nowhere close to what medium should be.

I understand mistakes happen, but for a premium priced cut like this, I expect more consistency and attention to detail. I hope the kitchen can take this feedback seriously, because everything else about the meal was wonderful just not the steak, which ironically was supposed to be the highlight.

author: Thida
review_text: AMAZING. I never leave reviews, but this experience was so special. I took my love out to celebrate his hard work, and our server Adam took such good care of us. The steaks were great, and the sides were even better, but note that you may want to order up on the level of doneness because our dry-aged ribeye was thick and came out a bit undercooked. No problem because Adam COMPED our dessert, the signature massive chocolate cake, which was the perfect level of sweetness. 10/10 would come here again.

author: Don Perry III
review_text: This place is incredible. The food was ridiculously good. The service was amazing. The drinks were delicious. The food, drinks, dessert and service make it worth the money. Will definitely be coming back here soon!
